editorial.headline: Trusts, Estates and Agency: Nationally Open, Closed to Bali PMA
editorial.standfirst: This activity can be wholly foreign-owned nationally, yet a foreign investor cannot register it at a Bali address under the province-wide PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
Foreign investors cannot register KBLI 64330 at a Bali address today. That conclusion sits beside—not against—its national position: the activity is nationally open to PMA, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. In Bali, the record identifies the large-scale activity as low risk and therefore caught by the island-wide, permanent PMA moratorium for all low and medium-low risk activities. The national ownership ceiling describes what is possible nationally; it does not secure a Bali registration.

At its centre, this is an activity for legal entities that assemble securities, estates and other financial assets for shareholders or beneficiaries, without managing those assets as a collective-investment scheme. The portfolio may be shaped toward a particular investment character—such as diversification, risk, return or price volatility—but the entity acts in the name of those with an interest in the assets. Its work can arise under the terms of a trust agreement, a will or an agency agreement. The scope also includes trusts, estates and similar financial entities, as well as family trusts that hold financial assets for individuals and families.

The activity has a deliberately particular economic profile. These entities receive interest, dividends and other property income, while having little or even no employment and no receipts from selling services. The scope also reaches shareholding companies that do not own or control equity, and venture companies funded solely through shares that do not charge fees. It is therefore a holding and beneficiary-facing structure, not a fee-driven operating business. Where income is earned by selling goods or services, that does not fit this activity’s stated scope.

Nationally, registration is open at the Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. That breadth should not obscure the Bali result. For a PMA applicant seeking a Bali address, the record’s status is blocked because the large-scale classification falls within the provincial moratorium’s low-risk coverage. The practical reading is crisp: national openness and full foreign ownership remain real features of this activity, but they do not override Bali’s island-wide PMA restriction.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness and full foreign ownership do not override Bali’s island-wide PMA restriction.
